reason: Confirmed by running the mutation. I extracted session/rich-steps to a private directory and moved the three-line writeStep(parent.id, 'delegate', ...) block in apps/server/src/modules/session/kernel.ts to after `await this.delegation.runBounded(...)`. Result: session tests 62 passed, 11 skipped. Whole suite: Test Files 38 passed, 10 skipped (48); Tests 449 passed, 97 skipped (546); zero failures. The skips are the Postgres-gated suites, so the reviewer's '546 passed' matches a run with a database. The only test of the new behaviour (kernel.test.ts:344, 'names in the delegate step exactly the tasks that step opened') filters the final snapshot by taskId and kind, so the position of the delegate step relative to the children's events is not observed. No test in the session slice subscribes to the broker and asserts that step.appended(delegate) comes before a child's task.status running or a child's step.appended. The scenario is reachable and user-visible: parts.tsx draws the children list only inside the delegate step (the `delegated` prop at lines 95 and 186, fed by tree.ts from detail.childTaskIds), so with the mutant the DELEGATED block on the live page is absent while the readers work, and appears only when all have finished. The comment at kernel.ts:212-214 states the ordering, and nothing holds it. Severity should-fix is correct: it is a test gap on the central behaviour of this commit, not a defect in the shipped code, so it is not a blocker. Sharpened fix: one kernel test that collects broker events during a delegate() with a worker that appends a child step, and asserts index(step.appended kind=delegate) < index(first child step.appended or task.status running). Cleanup done: the throwaway directory is removed, the stale worktree entry is pruned, the main working tree is untouched.
